title: Low-Degree Fourier Threshold for Random Boolean Functions
summary: We study whether a uniformly random Boolean function $f : \{-1,1\}^p \to \{-1,1\}$ is determined by its Walsh--Fourier coefficients of degree at most $d$. We show that the threshold lies at $p/2$ up to an $O(\sqrt{p \log p})$ window: if \[ d \le \frac{p}{2} - \sqrt{\frac{p}{2}\bigl(\log p + ω(1)\bigr)}, \] then with probability $1-o(1)$ there exists another Boolean function $g \ne f$ with the same degree-$\le d$ coefficients.
